title: Pagination
overview: Move through pages of a listing.
apply_when: A result or table set is split across pages.
not_when: Wizard steps (progress / task_list) or infinite scroll (no record yet).

vs.why: the rows; pagination is how you page them

role.overview: Move through a long list by page. Current page is named.
role.apply_when: A collection that does not fit one view.
role.not_when: Infinite scroll with no pager, or tabs.

size.overview: Highest in the size hierarchy — the easiest to hit.
size.apply_when: The view's main instance, or full-width on a small viewport.
size.not_when: A dense toolbar or a third option next to the main control.

size.apply_when: Ordinary use in forms, pages, and chrome.
size.not_when: The only control on a mobile screen that should span the width.

size.overview: Lowest in the size hierarchy — densest.
size.apply_when: Inline or chrome that sits beside content.
size.not_when: The page's primary instance, or a control under 44×44.

composition.overview: Previous and next, with or without page numbers.
composition.not_when: A load-more button that is not a pager (that is a button).

state.overview: A page other than this one is available.
state.apply_when: There is more than one page.
state.not_when: A pager on a single page of results.

state.overview: This page is the one they are on.
state.not_when: A visual fill with no aria-current.

state.overview: Previous or next is not available. Must stay perceivable.
state.not_when: A missing control with no explanation.

accessibility.overview: The pager is a named navigation (Pagination).
accessibility.not_when: A row of numbers with no nav name.

accessibility.overview: Previous/next name the destination, not only icons.

keyboard.overview: Tab lands on each available page control.
keyboard.not_when: The current page is a dead stop that traps.
